Oracle REST Data Services

Source: vignettes/oracle-ords.Rmd
oracle-ords.Rmd

Use oauth_db_oracle_ords_api() to read protected Oracle REST Data Services (ORDS) resources and call JSON handlers with each visitor’s OAuth token. It uses HTTPS without Oracle client libraries. For a native DBI connection, see Oracle Database.

Set up ORDS and sign-in

An ORDS administrator must REST-enable the required schema resources and protect them with ORDS privileges. Configure a JWT profile with the expected issuer, audience and signing keys. Map the token’s scopes or roles to the resource privileges. ORDS documents external-provider JWT profiles from release 23.3, including providers such as OCI IAM Identity Domains, Keycloak, Auth0 and Okta. Follow the ORDS authentication guide.

Register an authorization-code client with PKCE at the trusted provider and add http://localhost:8100 as a redirect URI. Configure the client to receive a JWT with the audience and access scope ORDS expects. Request OpenID Connect scopes for the Shiny sign-in. Enable refresh tokens when requesting offline_access, or use the provider’s documented alternative.

Save the app settings in .Renviron and restart R:

OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-shiny-app-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-shiny-app-client-secret
OAUTHDB_ORDS_ISSUER=https://login.example.org/realms/reporting
OAUTHDB_ORDS_SCOPE=reports.read
OAUTHDB_ORDS_URL=https://data.example.org/ords/reporting

Use the ORDS schema alias URL, including any reverse-proxy prefix. The example assumes that orders/ is a protected AutoREST collection. Register resources and database access rules before running it.

A complete app 

library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

scope <- Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_ORDS_SCOPE")
provider <- oauth_provider_oidc_discover(
  issuer = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_ORDS_ISSUER")
)
client <- oauth_client(
  provider,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  scopes = c("openid", "profile", "offline_access", scope),
  required_scopes = scope
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    verbatimTextOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  ords <- oauth_db_oracle_ords_api(
    auth$connection,
    url = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_ORDS_URL"),
    required_scopes = scope
  )
  output$rows <- renderPrint({
    ords$select("orders", query = list(limit = 20L))$items
  })
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*"),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

Save this as example.R, run source("example.R"), and open http://localhost:8100 in a regular browser. Sign in to read one page of the collection. Use offset and limit to page explicitly. Responses retain items, hasMore, offsets and links as native JSON lists; large JSON integers are strings. Server-provided links are never followed.

For a custom JSON handler, call its relative path:

result <- ords$request(
  c("api", "sales"),
  query = list(country = "NL"),
  trailing_slash = TRUE
)

select() appends a trailing slash for AutoREST collections. request() uses the path exactly, with trailing_slash = TRUE when the resource needs one. The client rejects redirects instead of sending credentials to a different endpoint. Use raw = TRUE to inspect a successful httr2 response. POST, PUT and PATCH can send a JSON body; the API is not a DBI connection or a SQL-result parser.

User identity and data access

ORDS validates the JWT and enforces its resource privileges. The JWT subject is available to handlers as :current_user. An ORDS role is not automatically an Oracle database role, and accepting a user JWT does not by itself change the database schema used by a handler. Configure handler filtering or a supported end-user security context to enforce the required per-user data access. Verify two users with different permissions before deployment.

Each operation gets a current token and stays tied to the authorization it started with. Responses arriving after sign-out or account replacement are discarded. GET and HEAD can refresh and retry once after HTTP 401. POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE are never replayed automatically. The client does not follow redirects or pagination links. It returns native JSON responses from custom handlers without interpreting application-specific success fields.

Automated tests mock ORDS responses and cover token renewal, scope checks, account isolation, routing, errors and request replay rules. No live ORDS or Oracle database was available for integration validation.
